one_liner: Saito and Matsumoto's 128-bit SIMD variant of the Mersenne Twister; about 2.3-2.8x faster than MT19937-64 for bulk 64-bit output.
what_it_does: A C library (SFMT.c plus headers) for a family of F2-linear generators with periods 2^607-1 to 2^216091-1. The Mersenne exponent is fixed at compile time with -DSFMT_MEXP (default 19937). The generator state lives in an sfmt_t struct. The API has sequential calls (sfmt_genrand_uint32/uint64/res53 and real1-3 conversions) and block calls (sfmt_fill_array32/64) that write straight into a caller array. It is not a drop-in for std::mt19937: the output sequence differs, and there is no C++ engine wrapper.
how_it_is_fast: The recursion works on 128-bit words (four 32-bit lanes) using only shifts, ANDs with a mask and XORs, so one SIMD instruction sequence produces 128 bits per step. The pick-up position (POS1=122 for 19937) and the lag-1/lag-2 feedback words (r1, r2) are chosen to keep dependency chains short. The block functions (sfmt_fill_array32/64) generate directly into the output array without copying the state. Since 1.5.2 an AVX2 path (SFMT-avx256.h, contributed by Masaki Ota) does two 128-bit steps per 256-bit operation and uses vpternlog under AVX-512VL. This relies on SL1 >= 16, so the dependent half-word term shifts out. A NEON path (SFMT-neon.h, optional SHA3 EOR3/BCAX) covers AArch64.
when_to_use: Bulk generation of 32-bit integers or doubles from an MT-family generator (Monte Carlo, simulation) where you can call sfmt_fill_array32/64 into a 16-byte-aligned buffer
Codebases that want a peer-reviewed, long-period (2^19937-1 or larger) F2-linear generator with jump-ahead for parallel streams (jump/ directory)
x86-64 with SSE2/AVX2 or AArch64 with NEON, where the SIMD path is enabled explicitly at build time
Replacing std::mt19937 when the exact MT19937 sequence does not matter but MT-style period and equidistribution analysis do
when_not_to_use: You need std::mt19937 / std::mt19937_64 bit-identical output (use a vectorized MT19937 such as VMT19937 instead)

64-bit integer output where high-dimensional equidistribution matters: Harase and Kimoto give SFMT19937-64 Delta=14095 vs 7820 for MT19937-64 and 0 for MELG19937-64. SFMT is tuned for 32-bit output, and dSFMT is the variant meant for doubles
Small-state or many-instance uses (per-thread or per-object generators): the 19937 state is SFMT_N = 156 128-bit words (about 2.5 KB), versus 256 bits for xoshiro256-class generators
Applications that care about TestU01 linearity tests: like all F2-linear generators, SFMT fails MatrixRank/LinearComp (per a search snippet, 4 of 106 BigCrush tests; source page not opened)
Big-endian or AltiVec targets: the README says these 'ARE NOT TESTED AT ALL'

integration.form: source-drop (SFMT.c + headers; CMakeLists.txt builds a static libSFMT.a)
integration.dependencies: none for the generator; the jump-ahead polynomial calculator (jump/calc-jump) needs NTL
integration.min_toolchain: C99 (Makefile uses -std=c99); gcc 3.4+ for SSE2 per howto-compile.html; MSVC supported via SFMT-sse2-msc.h; callable from C++ via extern "C"
integration.platforms: any (portable C path); SIMD paths for x86 SSE2, AVX2, AVX-512VL (256-bit), ARM NEON (AArch64 and ARMv7 Makefiles), PowerPC AltiVec (untested)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; since 1.4 all state is in a caller-owned sfmt_t, so one generator per thread is safe and sharing one needs external locking

gotchas: SIMD is off by default: you must pass -DHAVE_SSE2 (or HAVE_NEON / HAVE_ALTIVEC) plus the ISA flag, otherwise the plain C recursion is compiled even on x86-64. The AVX2 path is chosen automatically when __AVX2__ is defined together with HAVE_SSE2. CMake's USE_SSE2 passes -msse rather than -msse2.
SFMT_MEXP must be identical in every translation unit because it changes sizeof(sfmt_t); if it is missing, gcc warns and assumes 19937.

sfmt_fill_array32/64 require a 16-byte-aligned buffer on SIMD builds, a size that is a multiple of 4 (or 2) and at least SFMT_N32 (624) or SFMT_N64 (312) elements, and a freshly initialized or fully consumed state. They cannot be mixed with sequential calls without re-initializing, and gen_rand64 must not follow gen_rand32 (enforced only by assert).
howto-compile.html sample3 still uses the pre-1.4 global API (init_gen_rand, genrand_res53) that no longer exists; follow sample1/2 and SFMT.h instead.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick SFMT over VMT19937 or pXart when you do not need the std::mt19937 sequence and want the original authors' peer-reviewed SIMD design with jump-ahead and many period choices. Pick MELG-64 instead for 64-bit output with full equidistribution, and xoshiro-family SIMD generators (simdrng, Xoshiro256PlusSIMD) for small state and no linearity-test failures.
verified_claims_summary: In the README of Harase and Kimoto's ACM TOMS 2018 companion repo (melg-64), generating 1e9 64-bit integers with SIMD SFMT19937 took 1.8457 s vs 5.1002 s for the reference mt19937-64.c on a Core i7-3770, and 2.8806 s vs 6.6490 s on a Phenom II X6 1045T: about 2.8x and 2.3x (derived from page data). Both were built with gcc -O3 on Linux, gcc version not stated. Without SIMD, SFMT was only about 1.2x faster. The baseline is the original C reference, not libstdc++ std::mt19937_64.
status_note: Abandoned since 2021-05-18 (an open NEON update PR #10 from January 2026 is unmerged), but the 3-clause BSD code is small, stable since 2006 and easy to vendor.
